fluff.overview:
The Jenner is a relatively modern design, first constructed in 2784 by Diplan Mechyards of Ozawa under contract to House Kurita. Originally developed for the Star League Defense Force, the design was secretly acquired by the Draconis Combine after Kerensky's Exodus. Designed as a fast, hit-and-run guerrilla fighter, the Jenner would form the foundation for highly mobile lances that became a hallmark of DCMS doctrine.

Faster than most opponents while carrying respectable firepower for its weight class, the Jenner became synonymous with Combine military power, remaining the exclusive property of House Kurita for over fifty years. However, the Jenner's reputation was forever tarnished by its prominent role in the Kentares Massacre of 2796, when waves of Jenners carried out Coordinator Jinjiro Kurita's infamous directive.
fluff.capabilities:
Among the fastest 'Mechs of its era, the Jenner packs impressive firepower at close range. Its optimum engagement range is 30 to 90 meters, and its speed and jump capability make it exceptionally hard to hit. The Jenner can move in quickly, deliver its attack, and retreat before sustaining serious damage. Because the Argra 3L medium lasers are the primary armament, the 'Mech can operate for extended periods without ammunition concerns during deep raids.

The Thunderstroke SRM-4 provides additional hitting power for decisive moments, though the limited ammunition supply requires careful management during prolonged operations. Combined, these weapons give the Jenner more firepower than most light BattleMechs and several medium designs as well. Though an alpha strike generates significant heat, pilots use their impressive jump capability to buy cooling time between engagements.

The Jenner lacks arms for physical attacks, a deliberate design choice given its low tonnage. The four tons of armor provide only light protection compared to similar weight classes, making pilot skill and mobility essential to survival in sustained combat.
fluff.history:
Diplan was originally contracted by the SLDF to produce Jenners, with the first models joining the Exodus fleet in 2784. Once Kerensky disappeared, Kurita agents secretly negotiated with Diplan to continue the contract under the noses of FedSuns peacekeepers on Ozawa. When the DCMS began its offensive in 2786, Kurita MechWarriors infiltrated under civilian cover launched the first wave directly from Diplan's warehouses.

Despite the outbreak of the First Succession War, construction continued at Diplan Mechyard's factory on Ozawa until a raw materials shortage halted assembly in 2815, though chassis production continued. In 2823, production resumed on Ozawa, with some 3,000 chassis shipped to a Diplan subsidiary on Luthien for final fittings and assembly. By 2830, both production lines were producing 1,350 Jenners a year. The sheer destruction of the Succession Wars took their toll when the Ozawa facilities were destroyed in 2837, and unexplained explosion destroyed the remaining assembly plant on Luthien in 2848, ending Jenner production.

By 2840, the Federated Suns and Lyran Commonwealth had obtained operational Jenners through battlefield salvage. By 2845, all Successor States had access to the design, although it continued to be primarily a Kurita 'Mech. Despite the huge production volumes of the era, the Jenner never became very prevalent beyond the Draconis Combine. A favorite tactic of Jenner lances was to gang up on larger 'Mechs and unleash a devastating alpha strike, often with one or two 'Mechs equipped with inferno rounds.

Rebuilding a Jenner production line on Luthien became a top priority under Gunji-no-Kanrei Theodore Kurita. With ComStar aid, Luthien Armor Works finally reopened the line in 3046. The recovery of lost technology made the Jenner a prime candidate for upgrades, though LAW deliberately avoided radical changes to preserve the original's core advantages. The spectacularly brutal start to the Jihad led many units to return to stockpiles of once-shunned Jenners for replacement machines, proving their value once again.
fluff.deployment: This experimental variant uses a C3 boosted slave to share targeting data with enhanced range and reliability, cutting through electronic countermeasures that plagued standard C3 networks during the Jihad. Its weapons have been completely reconfigured, with a pair of MML-5 launchers replacing the standard armament, providing flexibility to load either long-range or short-range missile munitions as the tactical situation demands. Ten double heat sinks keep the chassis cool, while heavy ferro-fibrous armor increases protection over earlier models.
